sources.entry: scalene - A high-performance, high-precision CPU, GPU, and memory profiler for Python.

summary.one_liner: Scalene is a Python profiler that measures CPU, GPU, and memory usage per line and per function, with optional AI-generated optimization suggestions.
summary.what_it_does: Scalene samples running Python programs to report CPU time, split into Python, native (C/C++ library), and system time, with per-line and per-function breakdowns. It reports NVIDIA GPU time and per-line memory growth, copy volume, and likely memory leaks, using an included specialized memory allocator. It also attributes wall-clock await time in async code to the line where a coroutine is suspended, and shows stitched Python and native call stacks as flame charts and a timeline. Results are viewed in an offline web GUI, in the terminal, or as HTML, and a YAML config file can set options. Optional AI providers (Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Azure, OpenAI, Ollama) can suggest optimizations for a selected line or code region.
use_cases: find CPU hotspots in a slow Python script
track down memory growth and likely leaks
separate Python time from native library time
diagnose I/O bottlenecks in async code
notable: Separates Python-side time from native library time and system time, so you can see where optimization effort will pay off
Per-line memory profiling with a specialized allocator, including Python vs. native memory split and likely leak detection
AI-powered optimization proposals via GPT-4 and other providers, triggered by clicking a line or region in the GUI
Async profiling that shows per-line await time with mean and peak concurrency
Standalone self-contained HTML output that works offline
caveats: GPU profiling is limited to NVIDIA systems
AI suggestions need your own provider credentials or a local Ollama model
Windows memory profiling requires the Visual C++ Redistributable, and building from source needs Visual C++ Build Tools and CMake
Some PyTorch versions on Mac OS X interfere with Scalene, per the FAQ
keywords: why is my python script slow
